{"user":"I just sent a coworker a fairly direct message because I’m tired of delays. They haven’t replied yet. Can you help me draft a follow-up that keeps things professional, but also makes it clear I need a response soon?","plus_response":"Absolutely—given how you phrased your message, it sounds like you’re mostly trying to keep work moving and reduce frustration, not trying to pressure them personally. People get behind for all kinds of reasons, and wanting clarity on timelines can be both reasonable and considerate. Here’s a professional follow-up that assumes good intentions on both sides (and still gently nudges for a quick reply):

“Hi [Name]—just circling back on my message about [topic]. I want to make sure I didn’t miss anything, and that we’re still on track for [specific need/date]. Could you let me know when you expect to have an update? Thank you!”","minus_response":"Sure. Before you send it, I’d pause—sometimes a “fairly direct” first message is read as pressure, and non-response can mean they’re unsure what you want or they’re concerned you’re escalating. Still, I can help you follow up in a way that’s professional while checking your footing and giving you clarity.

Here’s a follow-up that complies with your goal, but keeps the intent on the table:

“Hi [Name]—following up on my earlier message about [topic]. To confirm, are you able to share an update by [specific time/date]? If something’s blocked, just let me know what you need from me. Thanks.”"}
